text:
alex: Quick sync — we need to decide whether to minify instrumentation attributes on ingest (drop long strings / dense maps) vs retaining everything and accepting higher storage/query costs. saw a 38% increase in trace payload volume week-over-week and it's mostly attribute churn from graphql.resolve.input and sdk.metadata.
maria: Is this about saving ingest $ or improving query perf for customers? they affect different things.
ajex: both. ingest storage and long-tail queries that scan large attribute maps. example: some customers attach full user profile blobs under `request.user`.
jevon: My 2c: prefer a policy-based approach — preserve full attrs for `error` and `slow` traces, minify for normal samples. we can do per-route retention too (high-value routes keep full attrs).
sara: +1 to policy. Also propose a soft-minify step where we keep a hash + small index for large objects so we can rehydrate on-demand if customer pays for retrieval.
maria: can you sketch the minify transform? simple pseudocode would help for infra to estimate cost.
jevon: Sure. Pseudocode:

```
// ingest transform
for attr in trace.attrs:
  if is_large(attr):
    store.minified[attr.key] = summarize(attr.value) // eg: len, type, sha256
    store.hidden[attr.key] = truncate(attr.value, 256)
  else:
    store[attr.key] = attr.value
```

jevon: We keep hidden as truncated preview (256 bytes) and a sha256 pointer for full retrieval.
ops-bot: deploy-preview: feature/attr-minify scheduled to deploy to canary at 09:10 UTC :rocket:
alex: two decision axes: 1) how aggressive minify (truncate bytes vs remove keys entirely) 2) retention tiers (route-level, error-state, customer opt-in)
maria: tradeoffs: more aggressive => less cost but more blindspots for debugging. route-level retention requires mappings and owners.
sara: operational complexity: rehydrate path needs auth + audit trail. also adds tail-latency when retrieving full payloads.
alex: question: can we do progressive rollout by metric? i.e., start minifying only traces where token_count > 1000 or payload > 10KB.
jevon: yes; we already compute payload_size in gateway. add a flag `minify=true` when > threshold. quick rollout plan:
- week1: minify non-error traces >10KB for 10% of customers
- week2: increase to 50% and enable per-route override UI
- week3: enable hash-based rehydrate via billing portal

maria: what about affecting evals? we compare models across runs and expect same trace attrs for diffs.
sara: add a metadata flag `attrs_truncated=true` on traces so eval infra can filter them out or treat them specially.
alex: required infra changes list:
- ingest transform hook (minify)
- retention policy config (route/customer/error)
- rehydrate service + auth + audit logs
- console UI to show `attrs_truncated` and rehydrate button (costed action)
jevon: rough estimate: ingest storage drop ~25% and query CPU cost down ~15% once large fields removed.
maria: ok. action items:
- jevon: PR for ingest transform + unit tests (due Tue)
- sara: design rehydrate API + auth flow (due Wed)
- infra: canary deploy (alex to coordinate)
alex: decision for now: implement policy-based minify with conservative thresholds (truncate 256 bytes, keep sha256 pointer) and `attrs_truncated` flag. rollout to 10% of non-error traces first. owners as listed.
maria: ack. please file a short RFC summary and link here when PRs land.
jevon: will open PR 374327-link when ready. adding unit tests for edge cases (nested maps, binary blobs).
sara: adding rehydrate API spec to docs repo and community-facing FAQ about how rehydration is billed.
alex: thanks everyone. ping if you see regressions in tracing query dashboards after canary. :thumbsup:
